title: The Effect of Acute Cognitive Stress on Sensorimotor Processing and Motor Learning
official: The Effect of Acute Cognitive Stress on Sensorimotor Processing and Motor Learning
summary:
The goal of this Pre-Post experimental interventional study is to determine whether acute cognitive stress may have a significant effect on how the brain processes information when learning a novel motor skill occurs immediately after acute stress.

The study is randomized two group parallel experimental design where participants will be randomly assigned to an acute stress group (induced via completion of an incongruent stroop task) as compared to a control group where participants will complete a comparator task (congruent stroop task).

Participants: will be healthy, right-handed dominant, male and female participants/volunteers aged 17-35.

Primary Research Question:

Does acute cognitive stress prior to learning a new motor skill change the way that the brain responds to acquisition of that skill? To answer this question, changes in the amplitude of somatosensory evoked potentials (SEPs) before and after participants acquire a motor skill will be compared between the acute stress and control group.

Secondary Research Questions:

1. Does acute cognitive stress prior to learning a new motor skill change the ability of the brain to acquire and retain that motor skill? To answer this question changes in the accuracy of a novel force matching task will be compared pre and post acquisition and at retention, measured 24 hours post acquisition between the acute stress and control group.
2. Does acute cognitive stress prior to learning a new motor skill change EEG measured prior to, during and post acquisition as compared to the control group?

Participants will complete the following procedures:

* Complete a pre-lab questionnaire screening to ensure eligibility criteria are followed, as well as signing an informed consent forum.
* EEG measures: a 64 channel EEG cap will be placed on the participant's head using the international 10/20 system. Resting state EEG measures will be collected, and EEG will be collected pre, during an post acquisition of the motor skill.
* SEP measures: Electrodes will be placed over the right median nerve, for the stimulation of the nerve at frequencies of 2.47Hz and 4.98Hz. In addition to the EEG cap to record cortical SEP measures, electrodes will be placed at specific places including Erb's Point, the Trachea, C5, etc, for recording of the spinal and peripheral SEP components.
* Participants in the acute stress group will complete an Incongruent Stroop Task while the control comparator group will complete a Congruent Stroop task. The goal of the task if to identify the colour of the font as quickly and correctly as possible. In the congruent condition the font will be in the same colour as the word e.g. the word will say "red" and the colour will be red. In the incongruent task, the colour and the word will be different, e.g. the word might say "blue" but the font colour will be red.
* Perform a novel force matching task with pre, acquisition, post and retention performance measures collected. To create an individualized force task, participants will first perform a a maximum voluntary contraction (MVC) to normalize the force matching task to their MVC, followed by a familiarization trial, and finally, randomized force matching acquisition trials across four varying blocks, followed by a post-acquisition block and retention measured 24 hours later.
* Participants will have their EEG and SEP recordings measured once again, after the Force Matching Handgrip Task, in accordance with study procedure.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* right handed males and females aged 17 to 35

Exclusion Criteria:

* left-handed

Conditions that may alter EEG suitability such as:

* multiple sclerosis
* epilepsy or seizure disorders
* serious head injuries
* Subclinical Neck Pain (SCNP) or recurrent neck pain
* Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD)
* ADHD
* Medications and substances can alter brain activity (identified via confidential screening questionnaire)
